title: Mantle · The armored collar
summary: Mantle is a lean biomechanical frame with a high segmented collar and exposed red upper arms. The latest head study pairs a faceted C-17 mask with a compact steel jaw inspired by the supplied Raiden portrait.

items.title: Mantle v003 · Faceted mask and articulated jaw
items.alt: Full-body Mantle beside an enlarged head study. The stamped mask has a flat crown, clipped corners and a dark temple strip. Blunt steel teeth extend down into a narrow chin plate between the separate collar guards.
items.body:
The mask has a short flat crown and clipped corners. A slim plate runs down one temple, echoing the overlapping collar guards. The front retains its worn C-17 stamp, four low slots and offset screw.

The blunt bite edges sit just below the mask. Each has a visible steel stem that seats in the chin plate. Small side links frame the jaw. The stems are longer and more exposed than in the supplied portrait, particularly at the center. The full-body view shows how much of the jaw reads between the collar guards at a distance.

**References used.** Both images were supplied directly to the built-in image generator. Mantle v002 supplied the chassis, collar and stamped face. The owner’s Raiden portrait supplied the relationship between the teeth, their roots and the lower jaw. [Mantle v002](assets/mantle/segmented-collar-v002.png) · [Raiden jaw reference](references/mantle/raiden-jaw-owner-reference.png)
items.prompt:
Faithful character concept edit for the game. Image 1 is the full design sheet for Mantle v002. Edit only the head in BOTH views on this sheet. Image 2 is the supplied Raiden portrait. Look closely at the small dark articulated metal teeth in the center beneath Raiden's lip and how their roots flow down into the chin. Use that relationship of tooth, socket and chin, translated into the existing mech. The body and the rest of Raiden's appearance are irrelevant. Deliver one landscape study with the SAME mech full-body at left and the enlarged near-frontal three-quarter head and collar at right. Dedicate most of the detail view to the head, include the full crown, open collar and a little chest. Use identical head geometry in both views. 

Make the jaw the focus: shorten the faceplate a little at the bottom to expose a narrow mechanical mandible. Immediately under the straight lower lip of the MASK, an intimate shallow arc of six to eight close-set gunmetal tooth mechanisms. As in Image 2, each presents a small blunt incisor-like dark contact face at the TOP and a longer individually shaped steel root or shank flowing DOWN and socketing into a small curved chin plate. A couple have a little circular recess near the root; two oblique side linkages suspend the mandible within the head. The center teeth have slightly broader flat biting edges and the outer ones narrow and turn back toward the cheeks. Show the vertical joins, the short dark line where the teeth meet the mask, and a fine cool highlight on each worn edge. Readable gunmetal with dark recesses and satin steel highlights, like a compact prosthetic jaw built for a machine. It should look subtly uncanny when you zoom in. Avoid a uniform row of pearls, a grille, exposed skull, lips, broad theatrical grin, chrome fangs or a giant lower jaw. Make this a visibly different jaw from image 1.

Alter the outer silhouette of the HEAD itself, modestly but visibly: shave the dome into a low near-flat crown with two sloped clipped corners. Short flatter temple planes on either side lead into a tapered chin. The front still has a subtly bowed, broad blank pewter faceplate, C-17 and weathered production marks, four quiet horizontal holes low on its face above the jaw, and one recessed off-center slotted screw. No human eyes, nose, eye-band, visor, horns or hair. Let one thin offset dark-metal overlapping temple strip echo the layered collar, sitting tight against one side and ending short of the jaw joint. No fussy fins. The overall head is compact, almost the same width as image 1, nested between the tall collar plates.

Keep the characteristic multipart shoulder collar, darker mechanical chest plates, slim waist, marked burgundy upper arms, long leg proportions, feet, worn industrial materials. Preserve exactly the two handheld and two independent back-mounted sci-fi weapons of Image 1 and hip jets; full figure fits the sheet, tips in frame. Neutral warm gray backdrop, natural directional studio light soft enough to reveal details in the dark jaw, no explanatory text, labels, borders or arrows.

items.title: Mantle v002 · Segmented collar and steel teeth
items.alt: Full-body front view and matching portrait of Mantle. Paired cheek guards rise inside separate shoulder caps. A close row of rounded steel teeth sits beneath the stamped mask. Overlapping chest plates frame a narrow waist.
items.body:
Each side of the collar has a tall inner cheek guard and a shorter outer plate. A dark gap exposes the round shoulder pivot below. The open front frames a single shallow row of small, rounded steel teeth. Their dark sides and silver highlights are clearest in the portrait.

A central access panel and overlapping steel ribs broaden the chest just above the flexible waist. Narrow strips of burgundy tissue show beneath the lower ribs. The marked upper arms and long leg muscles carry most of the red. The full figure shows both hand weapons, both raised back weapons and the side nozzles at the hips.

**References used.** The built-in image generator received both files directly. The Mantle sheet supplied the tooth profile, limbs and loadout. The Face study supplied the layered cheek guards and separate shoulder caps. [Mantle v001 front and back](assets/mantle/front-back-v001.png) · [Face study v003](assets/face-study/marked-mask-v003.png)
items.prompt:
Revise the fictional player mech MANTLE for a grounded grimdark videogame. Image 1 is Mantle v001 and governs the character, proportions, long lean legs, feet, red R04 upper arms, forearms, four weapons, stance, scale and materials. Image 2 is the earlier Face study: use its multipart collar construction, especially the close-up at left. Make one landscape sheet with two views of the SAME finished revision, on a quiet pale warm grey background. At left a complete almost straight-on full-body equipment view including feet and all four weapons. At right an enlarged, slightly oblique portrait from the crown to the lower ribs including the shoulder, collar, mouth and enough chest for them to be reviewed together. Same shape, tooth spacing and metals across both depictions. Clean studio lighting with a cool strip reflection across the jaw, sharp and readable like these references. No title, callouts or graphic embellishment.

1. From Image 1 preserve the tiny, close-set teeth immediately UNDER the chin of the oval stamped C-17 mask. Preserve the count, the shallow curved row, its small scale, rounded tips, spacing and the dark joint around them. Change ONLY their MATERIAL: each of these little tooth-shaped parts is made of polished hardened STEEL, with dark grey reflective faces, narrow cool silver glints, a few horizontal grinding marks. Their shapes give the impression of teeth up close as well as at a distance. Keep this subtle. No big locking bolts, sparse angular blocks, giant grille, gaps, fangs or cream enamel. Keep the four little black slots in the mask ABOVE the teeth exactly as before. Keep the asymmetrical cheek screw and worn serial stencils.

2. Make the multipart armored collar the signature of this chassis. Follow Image 2: close to the jaw is a pair of tall independent faceted cheek guards, a second set of slightly flared outer plates behind them, stepped edges and clear gaps to read the layers. Attach to the tops of the shoulder bearings with short visible dark links. Separate small overlapping shoulder caps ride on their own pivots, exposing the marked burgundy upper arms. The bits beside the head stand proud above those shoulder caps. Retain a broad shoulder-to-shoulder outline and leave the space in front of the chin open. These are physically distinct pieces with air, shadow and brackets between them, NOT a single curved metal yoke with cosmetic seam lines. Keep the collar more prominent than the chest.

3. Widen ONLY the ribcage of Image 1 modestly, about 12–15%, preserving the lean waist, shoulder span, hips and limb lengths. Give it a shallow faceted gunmetal sternum service cover flanked by two overlapping, gently angled bands of metal rib armor per side. Broader dark steel surfaces across the upper torso with burgundy fibers appearing only in narrow side openings toward the obliques. Leave a flexible mechanical waist. The torso should read predominantly as a worn machine with tissue behind it, and stay appreciably narrower than the collar. No enormous breastplate, no thick new shoulder pads, no superhero abs. Keep the exposed red R04 upper arms, and the major red thigh and calf bundles from source 1, so the organic material feels deliberate.

Full figure carries the same long slim sci-fi accelerator in the mech's right hand, short wide emitter in its left, high outboard box missile cassette above its right shoulder and folded twin rail above its left, each back unit on its own visible hinge attaching behind the collar. Keep outer hip side-jet nozzles and low rear boosters in place. Hands closed on grips. Check all four weapons visually. Plenty of margin around feet and weapon tips, industrial product painting with restrained weathering, matching camera height to the references, no other characters or redesign of the legs.

items.title: Mantle · Front and back
items.alt: Front and back views of Mantle. A broad curved steel collar spans the shoulders above lean red arms, ribs, waist and legs. Two hand weapons and two back mounts are visible.
items.body:
The collar dips below the chin and sweeps in one arc to the pinned ends over both shoulder bearings. Beneath the overhang, the white R04 stencil follows the exposed upper-arm fibers. The forearms have simple guards. Red fibers wrap the ribs, waist, thighs and calves around a narrow mechanical core.

A long accelerator and a short emitter occupy the hands. Behind the collar, a cassette and twin-rail unit mount on separate pivots above the low rear boosters. The side nozzles sit outside the hips. The proposed gait is upright and narrow: on a lateral boost the hips move under the collar, then the leading foot catches the weight.

The rounded tooth row on this first sheet is the shape selected for the next revision. [See the steel treatment in v002](assets/mantle/segmented-collar-v002.png). [Open full-resolution PNG](assets/mantle/front-back-v001.png)

**References used.** Both images were supplied directly to the built-in image generator. Face study v003 supplied the head markings, slotted hardware, red upper arms and four weapon positions. The full-body portrait informed the tapered torso and tissue meeting the arms. [Face study v003](assets/face-study/marked-mask-v003.png) · [Full-body portrait](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-full-body-788411478568840781.jpg) · [Original pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840781/)
items.prompt:
Transform the project mech in IMAGE 1 into MANTLE, its own lean purpose-built chassis. Produce a landscape industrial character design sheet: a large full-body front three-quarter view with an easy-to-read face, plus a smaller rear three-quarter view of the exact same machine. The two forms must be visually different from the box-bodied ancestor. Use IMAGE 1 for only the marked oval head, the striated red UPPER ARMS between shoulder and elbow, the founding team's build quality, and four weapon interfaces. IMAGE 2 informs a tapered, almost human silhouette and the fluid transitions between hard surfaces and fibers. Do not import its head spikes, dress, or horns.

THE DESIGN'S IDENTIFYING SHAPE is ONE broad, rigid, open-front shoulder-to-shoulder armor collar. Think of a heavy pressed-metal gorget enlarged until it spans the entire clavicle line of a lean sprinter. The middle rises along the sides behind the jaw; the two lips flare smoothly OUTWARD and then DOWN to short articulated plates pinned directly over the left and right shoulder bearings. From the front it makes one continuous sweeping crescent around a small, calm head with a deep notch under the chin. From behind it forms a simple continuous metal arc running between the shoulder pins. Use big uninterrupted planes of scuffed desaturated warm gunmetal, visibly thick turned edges, large inset fasteners and a dark shadow underneath to show its mass. The collar alone carries this big metal silhouette. It protects just the neck and tops of the shoulders. No giant chest breastplate or separate bulbous shoulder pads, no cloth cape. The lower shoulder socket and the UPPER ARM are deliberately exposed and plainly visible in the frame below the lip.

Under this distinctive armor build a distinctly SLIM almost human-shaped full body: narrow oval ribcage with real depth for a pilot, tapered waist, long lean upper limbs with elbows at waist height and wrists at high thigh, human-pattern pelvis, well-supported long thighs and calves, useful split steel heels and feet. Strong but lithe rather than skeletal or heroic bodybuilder. The broad collar and bare slim waist must make a new instantly recognizable silhouette. MOST of the body below the collar reads as deep oxblood biomechanical tissue with limited near-black joint hardware and narrow protective splints. Fine parallel red contractile bands curve around each steel upper-arm bearing with the white R04 stencil and inset round fastener from image 1. Oblique red fans wrap the sides of the ribs into the waist, larger fans form the outside of each thigh, with narrow wrapped fibers at the Achilles. Red tissue under load in the side and legs. Integrated dark mechanical core and human-scale hatch recessed along a flank. Compact plain forearm braces and mechanical grippers; don't enlarge the forearms. No raw gore or human skin, superhero suit, six-pack breastplates, or separate patches stuck onto armor.

Keep the original clean stamped pewter mask tucked low inside the oversized collar; interrupted batch marks, C-17, small low punched openings and a single recessed slotted cheek screw. Beneath the chin replace every rounded ivory tooth with FLAT graphite-colored rectangular locking lugs around a mechanical neck bearing. Show worn silver glints on only a few edges, an interrupted straight machining pattern. This might register as teeth from afar. Close up it's clearly metal.

Exactly four durable, swappable mech-scale weapons in EACH view: a long slim angular accelerator in the anatomical right hand and a short broad pulse projector in the left, visibly gripped. A shallow rectangular missile cassette on the right back and a folded slim twin-rail unit on the left back each attach to an independent exposed hinge on rails rooted on the narrow chassis just behind the collar. The gun units are outboard, with generous air between them and the head; keep the collar's whole sweep visible in front. Full-size industrial sci-fi weapons, never a human-sized pistol. Two low rear booster bells and small side nozzles on the outer hips, especially clear from the rear. Closed rear panel of missile cassette towards rear camera. Credible landing stance with easy room for elbows, legs and exhaust. One rear mount raised so the eye can see the connection to the back. Same configuration in both angles, respect actual fore/aft geometry.

Neutral gray-beige field and soft directional studio light, slightly weathered materials, dim rich burgundy with cool steel; confident design painting with clear spatial silhouettes, a little spare space all around both views. Study camera near torso height so the slim proportions read true. Complete feet, weapons and collar fitted inside canvas in both views. No dramatic lighting, captions, labels, title or story decoration.

items.title: Collar and neck bearing · Detail
items.alt: Close-up of Mantle’s stamped mask. Three flat steel lugs project from a dark neck bearing above the continuous shoulder collar and its round pins.
items.body:
**Set aside after review.** The three square blocks changed the tooth shape too much. The requested revision returns to the small rounded row on the front-and-back sheet and changes its material to steel. [See v002](assets/mantle/segmented-collar-v002.png).

Three widely spaced steel lugs catch the light below the mask. The dark track continues around the side of the head. From the front those few silver edges suggest teeth; this view shows their square flanks and the cut of the bearing. The collar arches over the red upper arm, leaving room for it to rotate beneath the armor.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/mantle/collar-detail-v001.png)

**Reference used.** The [Mantle front and back sheet](assets/mantle/front-back-v001.png) was supplied directly to the built-in image generator for this revision. It established the stamped face, shoulder-to-shoulder armor and marked tissue. The flat locking lugs refine the earlier jaw detail.
items.prompt:
Using the supplied Mantle full-body design sheet as the exact character reference, paint ONE enlarged three-quarter maintenance portrait of the same head, broad armored gorget and near shoulder, cropped around the upper ribs and outer upper-arm bearing. A companion detail on the same neutral ground, same scuffed dark warm-gray metal, readable shapes and russet striated tissue. Keep its distinctive broad single wraparound shoulder-bridging collar with big circular pinned ends, the little stamped C-17 pewter mask and its four small dark front slots, the cheek screw and the exposed R04 red upper arms. Only the interface immediately under the mask is redesigned in this detail.

There is absolutely no anatomical lower jaw under the mask. Give the mask an underside like the flat underside of a turret on a turntable. Under that edge show a dark horizontal steel race with an inner stepped flange. Interrupt the flange with THREE or FOUR widely spaced, dead-flat squared metal locking dogs. Their forms are visibly mechanical: each is cut from the same graphite-steel ring, rectangular milled flanks, horizontal chamfer, flat faces, deep rectangular gaps; one broad tang goes behind the collar side. Worn silver on the top corner of each catches the light. The camera sees the stepped ring continue around the near side of the neck as the face turns fifteen degrees. Keep the front slots ABOVE this structure. From a distance the glints could be mistaken for teeth, but zoomed in the track, gaps and dark squared blocks must be legible as machine parts. No enamel, bone white, rounded teeth, lips, gums, skeletal jaw, fangs, smile, dense grille, row of tiny receding pegs.

Use the composition to show the relation of the continuous thick armored rim to the little mask and red upper arm. Camera slightly below the cheek, enough surrounding shoulder arc for context. Broad soft angled side light, realistic industrial material study, precise machining visible, not exploded, no labels, arrows, extra vignettes, logos, dramatic lighting or captions. The back weapons can fall outside this close crop.
